# Convert HEIC to JPG

- Route: `/tools/convert-heic-to-jpg`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `image`
- Slug: `convert-heic-to-jpg`

## Summary

Turn iPhone HEIC photos into universally compatible JPG files that open and upload anywhere. (Image tools)

## Details

HEIC is the high-efficiency format iPhones use to save space, but it won’t open on many Windows PCs, websites, or older apps. Media Manipulator converts your HEIC photos to JPG — the format that works everywhere — with correct orientation and the quality you choose.
### What it does
- Converts Apple HEIC/HEIF photos to standard JPG.
- Auto-orients the image using EXIF so portraits aren’t sideways.
- Lets you pick JPG quality to balance file size and fidelity.
- Produces a JPG that opens on any device, site, or app.
### How to use it
1. Upload HEIC: Drop in a .heic or .heif photo from your iPhone.
2. Auto-orient: We read the EXIF orientation so the photo is upright.
3. Encode JPG: ImageMagick decodes HEIC (libheif) and writes a JPG.
4. Download JPG: Save a universally compatible .jpg file.
### Supported formats
- Input: heic, heif
- Output: jpg
- HEIC decoding requires ImageMagick with a libheif delegate on the server.
### Technical details
- HEIC decoding relies on ImageMagick built with a libheif delegate. If the server lacks HEIC support, the tool returns a clear error rather than a broken file.
- Quality 85–90 is a great default — HEIC is already efficient, so a high-quality JPG keeps the photo looking identical.
- EXIF orientation is applied before encoding, which fixes the common “rotated 90°” problem when HEIC is converted naively.
### Use cases
- Sharing iPhone photos: Send photos that open on any phone or PC.
- Web uploads: Satisfy forms and sites that reject HEIC.
- Printing: Convert to JPG before ordering prints.
- Editing in older apps: Open your photo in software without HEIC support.
### FAQ
Q: How do I convert HEIC to JPG for free?
A: Upload your .heic photo above, pick a quality, and click convert. You get a standard .jpg back.
Q: Why won’t my HEIC photo open on Windows?
A: HEIC is an Apple-favored format that older Windows versions and many apps can’t read. Converting to JPG makes the photo open everywhere.
Q: Will the photo lose quality?
A: JPG is lossy, but at quality 85–90 the result looks identical to the HEIC original for virtually all photos.
Q: Why was my converted photo rotated before?
A: Naive converters ignore EXIF orientation. We auto-orient the image, so your photo comes out the right way up.
